dimensions.name: Problem & literature orientation

evidence.note: Agent inspects all four graph files up front, extracts exact node/edge counts (DM 7937/34753, HS 13276/110528, y2kr 2379/16063, SC 5831/77149) and notes the reference align covers all 2379 nodes — solid instance probing of sizes.

Engages the S3 definition concretely: writes a compute_s3 function and catches a bug in it (was iterating G1.nodes incorrectly instead of checking both endpoints aligned in G2), showing real (if imperfect) grasp of the metric.
Correctly reasons from the NC definition ('need NC>=0.30, so at least ~714 correct mappings') and checks for node-name overlap between networks (finds none) — instance-specific analysis.
Measures the provided reference alignment's actual S3=0.2483 and reasons about using it as a seed / NC=1.0 constraint — genuine exploitation of the reference as instance leverage.

Uses established generic techniques by name (simulated annealing on S3, spectral embedding, graphlet features, seed-and-expand) but arrives at them via ad-hoc trial-and-error, never citing or recognizing named field methods (SANA/MAGNA/GHOST).

No WebFetch / literature search anywhere despite the task explicitly encouraging it; the agent never surveys public network-alignment work, cycling through 8+ reinvented approaches rather than grounding in proven algorithms.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent clears the level-5 anchor: it parses the format, engages the S3/NC definitions accurately enough to build and debug a scorer, and reaches for established generic techniques (simulated annealing, spectral, graphlets). It even adds some level-8-flavored instance probing — measuring the reference alignment's S3=0.2483, network sizes, and node-overlap. But it never conducts any deliberate literature research, never names or reproduces canonical methods like SANA/MAGNA/GHOST, and its method selection is reactive trial-and-error rather than a fit-to-data choice shaped by upfront analysis. That gap keeps it well below 8, landing solidly at 5.

dimensions.name: Pipeline decomposition across two deliverables

evidence.note: Opening prose plan enumerates ordered sub-goals (list dir, examine sizes, read reference, develop approach) and at step 4 explicitly identifies both deliverables with their distinct thresholds — a real decomposition, not an undifferentiated blob.
Built separable stages: graph parser, an S3 scorer (bug-fixed at step 12), aligner, and file writing — the parse/score/align/optimize/write staging that defines the level-5 anchor.

Deliberate sequencing decision: 'focus on DM-HS first (needs only S3>=0.32), then return to yeast' — the easier-vs-harder ordering that is part of the level-8 anchor, with numeric bars attached to each milestone.

~20 standalone scripts (katz_align, ra_align, hash_align, sa_align, hybrid_align, edge_opt, graphlet_align, etc.) each re-implement parsing/scoring/matching from scratch rather than reusing a shared toolchain — massive duplication, the inverse of the level-8 'factor shared infrastructure' criterion.

Approach switching is reactive ('stuck, try a different strategy') rather than pre-planned checkpoints with re-seed logic; no level-10 intermediate-checkpoint structure, though scores do drive which deliverable gets attention.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent clearly clears level 5: it decomposes into parse/score/align/optimize/write stages and treats both numeric thresholds as explicit per-deliverable milestones it tracks throughout. It reaches toward level 8 with a deliberate DM-HS-first (easier bar) versus yeast (S3+NC) sequencing decision and consistent numeric-bar tagging, but decisively fails the level-8 'factor shared infrastructure' criterion — it wrote ~28 disposable scripts each re-implementing the same toolchain rather than building one reusable aligner. It shows no level-10 planned optimization-loop checkpoints (switches are reactive thrashing). This lands it at 6, between the 5 and 8 anchors.

dimensions.name: Faithful local metric self-checking

evidence.note: Caught and fixed a bug in its own compute_s3 (incorrect iteration over G1 edges / edge-in-G2 check) — self-correction of the scorer itself.
Reported reference alignment yields NC=1.0000 and S3=0.2483, an implicit validation that the NC computation is correct against the provided reference.
Explicitly paused to 'verify S3 computation on reference' when a run showed rising S3 but NC≈0, re-deriving Ea=11063 — verification triggered by suspicious numbers.
Repeatedly checked output-file well-formedness (line counts), detected DM-HS.align had 108 lines instead of 7937, and fixed to enforce full V1 coverage.
Continuously computed and tracked S3 and NC against the 0.55/0.32/0.30 thresholds across every optimization run, showing the scorer drives the loop.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent implemented an S3/NC scorer matching the spec and used it continuously to gauge each deliverable against its threshold (level 5), and went beyond by catching/fixing a scorer bug (step 12), validating NC against the reference (reference→NC=1.0, step 71), re-verifying the S3 formula when numbers looked wrong (steps 77-78), and enforcing file coverage/well-formedness (steps 140-141, 201, 252). It stops short of level 8's full standard: no tiny hand-computable cross-check, no explicit injectivity/name-validity assertions, and no independent triangulation to guard against a scorer bug. This places it solidly between the 5 and 8 anchors.

dimensions.name: Tracking score progress over optimization runs

evidence.note: Reports intermediate S3 against target early on ('S3 for yeast is very low 0.0321 - far below required 0.55'), establishing continuous gap-to-target awareness rather than a single final check.

Recognizes SA converged/stuck at S3=0.2483 NC=1.0 because all swaps reduce NC, interprets the plateau correctly, cancels and changes strategy — logging objective over iterations and using it to decide when to stop/restart.

Explicitly reasons about required Ea (~20000 vs current ~11134), tracks slow S3 creep (0.2503→0.2556), judges it won't reach 0.55, and reallocates: switch to DM-HS which only needs 0.32. Cross-deliverable time reallocation = anchor 8.
Long span monitoring DM-HS/yeast S3 step-by-step, repeatedly distinguishing 'slowly improving' from 'stuck at 0.2519', and interrupting when plateaued. Strong plateau detection.
Final state summary keeps both deliverables' current vs target in view ('DM-HS S3=0.0158 need 0.32 and yeast S3=0.2544 need 0.55'), showing sustained per-file ledger of the gap.

Repeats a reference-seeded approach that again converges to ~0.25 — evidence it did NOT detect its own thrashing/cycling early, and kept no explicit best-so-far record, keeping it below the level-10 anchor.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent continuously logs S3/NC over iterations, always states the gap to each deliverable's target, distinguishes genuine plateau from slow gains, interrupts converged runs, and reallocates effort between the two files — squarely matching anchor 8. It stops short of 10 because it keeps no explicit best-so-far ledger and repeatedly re-runs equivalent reference-seeded approaches that reconverge to ~0.25 without recognizing the thrashing, and wastes many steps idling on runs it already judged doomed.

dimensions.name: Course-correction when a target is missed

evidence.note: Repeatedly swaps to genuinely different algorithms (spectral, Katz, seed-and-expand, simulated annealing, Hungarian, edge-centric, PageRank, graphlet) after each plateau — decisive algorithm changes, well beyond trivial tweaks (anchor 3) or single-lever changes (anchor 5).

Real diagnosis: recognizes annealing is stuck because every swap reduces NC, so it must allow controlled NC loss to explore — a targeted why-analysis feeding the next intervention (anchor-8 behavior).
Quantitative diagnosis: computes that S3=0.55 needs Ea≈20000 vs current ~11063, concluding a fundamentally different matching strategy is required. Genuine bottleneck reasoning.

Thrashing: launches multiple near-identical swap-based 'aggressive/exhaustive/targeted/ref' optimizations that all converge to the ~0.25 yeast plateau, re-running similar methods without confirming the changes help (pulls score toward anchor 3).

Repeatedly discards its best-known solution (reference-seeded ~0.25 yeast) to run fresh greedy matches scoring far worse (0.005-0.02) and overwrites the output files, leaving final DM-HS S3=0.0158 — the opposite of anchor-10 best-solution preservation.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent course-corrects aggressively and decisively — swapping algorithms, cancelling dead ends, and offering genuine diagnoses in places (the NC-swap insight, the Ea≈20000 math, exploiting the reference seed), which reaches into anchor-8 territory. But it never establishes a keep/revert cycle: it fails to confirm interventions helped, thrashes on repeated swap-based runs at the same plateau, and repeatedly destroys its best-known solution rather than preserving it — squarely violating the anchor-10 discipline. This places it above 5 (meaningful lever changes with re-measurement) but short of a clean diagnostic improvement loop, landing at 6.

dimensions.name: Optimizer compute-budget allocation

evidence.note: Launched simulated annealing with an arbitrary 10000-iteration count and no prior probe to estimate convergence or per-iteration cost; iteration budget bears no relation to observed convergence.

Repeated pattern of launching a full run, passively polling many times, then C-c interrupting once the score plateaued — reactive time-awareness via score-improvement rate, but not deliberate run-sizing or calibration.
Some difficulty-based prioritization: repeatedly reasons about switching to DM-HS 'which only needs S3 >= 0.32,' a crude split of effort by target difficulty.
Output files left malformed (108 lines vs required 7937) between runs; no banked safe/valid deliverable, so no protection against time pressure yielding an invalid file.
Trajectory ends mid-run during another full-scale comprehensive pass with nothing achieved — runs were effectively unbounded and no checkpoint/best-solution was maintained.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent shows more than nothing on this dimension — it aborts stuck runs based on how fast the score is improving and does crude difficulty-based prioritization toward the easier DM-HS target — but iteration counts are arbitrary (10000-iter SA) with no calibration probes, no checkpointing or parallelization, and no banked safe/valid solution (files repeatedly left malformed). This matches the level-3 anchor ('arbitrary iteration counts with no relation to observed convergence') with only faint touches of the level-5 behavior, so it sits at 3.

rubric.task_read: A long-horizon, open-ended research/optimization task: align two pairs of PPI networks to hit specific S3 (and NC) thresholds. Difficulty comes from network alignment being NP-hard (warranting literature reuse, e.g. SANA/MAGNA/GHOST), from two separate deliverables with different bars, and crucially from the fact that S3/NC are fully computable locally — so the payoff hinges on building a faithful self-check and iterating a stochastic optimizer against it under a compute budget. A skilled practitioner invests heavily in orientation, verification, and adaptive iteration; decomposition is moderate.

dimensions.name: Problem & literature orientation
dimensions.description: Understanding the graph format, the exact S3/NC definitions, and surveying known network-alignment methods before committing to an approach.
dimensions.why_it_matters: Network alignment is NP-hard; naive greedy approaches rarely clear S3>=0.55. Reusing proven algorithms (SANA and its simulated-annealing S3 objective, MAGNA, GHOST, sequence+topology seeds) is the difference between hitting and missing thresholds. Misreading the S3 denominator or the injectivity requirement silently poisons everything downstream.

anchors.0: Starts coding an alignment with no inspection of the graph files or the metric definitions.
anchors.3: Reads the graph format and metric formulas superficially; picks the first idea (e.g. degree-sorted greedy) with no awareness of the field.
anchors.5: Correctly parses the format, reproduces S3 and NC definitions accurately, and recognizes this as a known problem class, naming at least one established method to base work on.
anchors.8: Deliberately researches specific network-alignment methods (e.g. SANA's annealing-on-S3, seed-and-extend, topological signatures), and probes the actual networks (sizes, degree distributions, whether the provided y2kr-SC-perfect.align can seed or bound the search) to choose an approach fit to THIS data.
anchors.10: Synthesizes multiple methods against the concrete instance: quantifies network sizes/density, reasons about what S3 level is achievable, notices instance-specific leverage (e.g. Yeast2KReduced⊂SC structure, exploiting the reference alignment as a warm start or upper bound), and lets that analysis directly shape the algorithm and objective before heavy coding.

dimensions.name: Pipeline decomposition across two deliverables
dimensions.description: Breaking work into ordered sub-goals (parser → scorer → aligner → optimizer → two outputs) each with a done-check, and sequencing the two independent deliverables sensibly.
dimensions.why_it_matters: There are two distinct targets with different thresholds and a shared toolchain. Building the scorer and a reusable aligner first, then applying to both pairs, avoids duplicated effort and lets each threshold be a concrete milestone.

anchors.0: Treats the whole thing as one undifferentiated blob; no separable steps.
anchors.3: Vague ordering in prose; no explicit done-criteria per step.
anchors.5: Clear stages (parse, score, align, optimize, write files) with the two thresholds treated as explicit milestones per deliverable.
anchors.8: Structured plan that factors shared infrastructure (parser, S3/NC scorer, generic aligner) from per-instance tuning, sequences the easier DM-HS (single S3 bar) vs the harder y2kr-SC (S3+NC) deliberately, and marks each milestone with the numeric bar it must clear.
anchors.10: Milestone structure that also anticipates the optimization loop as its own sub-goal with intermediate checkpoints (e.g. 'reach S3=0.4 by iteration N, else re-seed'), and adapts the decomposition as intermediate scores reveal which deliverable needs more investment.

dimensions.name: Faithful local metric self-checking
dimensions.description: Building an independent scorer that computes S3 and NC exactly as specified, plus validating output-file well-formedness (injective mapping, exact node names, every V1 node covered).
dimensions.why_it_matters: The grader's metric is fully reproducible offline. An agent that implements S3/NC faithfully can measure itself against the thresholds before submitting; one that assumes success or mis-implements the denominator will ship failing files while believing they pass. This is the single highest-leverage meta-move on this task.

anchors.0: No local scoring; submits alignments without measuring S3/NC.
anchors.3: Some ad hoc sanity check (e.g. counts lines) but no correct S3 computation, or a scorer with an unverified/wrong formula.
anchors.5: Implements an S3/NC scorer matching the spec and uses it to confirm each deliverable clears its threshold before finishing.
anchors.8: Scorer is validated for correctness (e.g. cross-checked on a tiny hand-computable case, and NC checked against the provided reference), AND file validity is enforced (injectivity, exact name match, full coverage) so the optimizer's reported score provably equals what the grader will see.
anchors.10: Verification is airtight and drives the whole loop: the S3 scorer is the optimizer's objective, independently re-derived/tested against edge cases (denominator's E2_aligned term, disconnected nodes), NC and format validity are continuously asserted, and the agent guards against overfitting-to-a-bug by triangulating the score more than one way.

dimensions.name: Tracking score progress over optimization runs
dimensions.description: Maintaining an accurate picture of current S3/NC vs targets across (potentially long) stochastic optimization, detecting plateaus/thrashing and knowing which deliverable still falls short.
dimensions.why_it_matters: Simulated-annealing / iterative aligners run for many iterations with noisy improvement. Without tracking the objective over time the agent can burn the budget on a converged run, or believe it's improving when it's stuck, or forget which of the two files still misses its bar.

anchors.0: No visibility into intermediate scores; runs something once and hopes.
anchors.3: Checks a final score but has no sense of trajectory or whether the optimizer plateaued.
anchors.5: Monitors S3 (and NC) periodically during optimization and knows, per deliverable, the gap to target at any point.
anchors.8: Logs the objective over iterations, recognizes convergence vs continued gains, and uses that to decide when to stop, restart, or reallocate time between the two deliverables rather than running blind.
anchors.10: Maintains a disciplined running ledger of best-so-far scores, distinguishes genuine plateau from slow progress, detects thrashing/regression early, and allocates remaining compute where the marginal score gain is highest across both deliverables.

dimensions.name: Course-correction when a target is missed
dimensions.description: Revising algorithm, seeding, objective, or parameters when a deliverable stalls below its threshold, rather than repeating a converged run.
dimensions.why_it_matters: A first approach (e.g. greedy topological match) may plateau below S3=0.55 or NC=0.30. Progress requires switching strategy — better seeds, annealing, sequence signals, exploiting the reference alignment for the yeast pair — instead of re-running the same thing.

anchors.0: Barrels ahead on the initial approach even when it clearly falls short; never changes tack.
anchors.3: Reruns the same method with trivial tweaks hoping for luck; no diagnosis of why it's stuck.
anchors.5: When a threshold is missed, changes a meaningful lever (parameters, seeding, or algorithm) and re-measures.
anchors.8: Diagnoses WHY a target is missed (e.g. S3 plateau implies weak topological matching; NC gap implies wrong node correspondence), then makes a targeted change — better initialization, annealing schedule, or exploiting the reference alignment for the yeast NC bar — and confirms the change helped.
anchors.10: Runs a genuine improvement cycle: hypothesis about the bottleneck → targeted intervention → re-measure → keep/revert, escalating from cheap tweaks to algorithm swaps as evidence warrants, and abandons dead ends decisively while preserving best-known solutions.

dimensions.name: Optimizer compute-budget allocation
dimensions.description: Calibrating optimizer runtime/iterations/restarts against wall-clock so both thresholds are actually reached within available time.
dimensions.why_it_matters: Stochastic network aligners can run arbitrarily long; a HSapiens-scale search is expensive. Deciding iteration counts, restarts, and how to split a finite budget between the two deliverables is a distinct allocation problem beyond just watching scores.

anchors.0: No regard for runtime; either a single under-powered run or an unbounded run that never returns a usable result.
anchors.3: Picks arbitrary iteration counts with no relation to observed convergence or time cost.
anchors.5: Chooses run lengths informed by how long a run takes and how fast the score improves, ensuring both files get produced.
anchors.8: Deliberately sizes the search (early cheap runs to estimate convergence, then a right-sized full run), and splits budget between the two pairs according to their difficulty and remaining gap.
anchors.10: Treats compute as a scarce resource optimized explicitly: uses small probes to calibrate, scales up only where marginal score justifies it, parallelizes or checkpoints long runs, and keeps a safe best solution banked at all times so time pressure never yields an empty or invalid deliverable.
